definitions.gloss: main hall of a Shinto shrine
definitions.explanation: The innermost and most sacred building of a Shinto shrine, which houses the enshrined deity (御神体). Visitors typically worship at the worship hall (拝殿) in front, as the main hall is usually not open to the public.

examples.japanese: {本殿|ほんでん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{国宝|こくほう}→国宝：09642_kokuhou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{指定|してい}→指定：00373_shitei⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The main hall is designated as a national treasure.
Behind the main hall stands an old cedar tree.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{本殿|ほんでん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{室町時代|むろまちじだい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{建|た}てられた→建てる：01189_tateru⟧もので、⟦{歴史的|れきしてき}→歴史的：05671_rekishiteki⟧⟦{価値|かち}→価値：00131_kachi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{非常|ひじょう}→非常：01598_hijou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧。
examples.english: The main hall of this shrine was built during the Muromachi period and has extremely high historical value.

notes:
USAGE:
{本殿|ほんでん} refers specifically to the main building of a Shinto shrine (⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧), where the ⟦{御神体|ごしんたい}→御神体：23465_goshintai⟧ (sacred object representing the deity) is housed. It is distinct from the ⟦{拝殿|はいでん}→拝殿：24252_haiden⟧ (worship hall), where visitors pray.

The {本殿|ほんでん} is typically located behind the ⟦{拝殿|はいでん}→拝殿：24252_haiden⟧ and is often not accessible to the general public.

For Buddhist temples, the equivalent term is ⟦{本堂|ほんどう}→本堂：15935_hondou⟧ (main hall).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {本殿|ほんでん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{参拝|さんぱい}する→参拝する：15627_sanpaisuru⟧: to worship at the main hall
- {本殿|ほんでん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{建築|けんちく}→建築：02709_kenchiku⟧⟦{様式|ようしき}→様式：05455_youshiki⟧: architectural style of the main hall
- ⟦{国宝|こくほう}→国宝：09642_kokuhou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{本殿|ほんでん}: a main hall designated as a national treasure
